podcast.title: Erratic Behavior and Asperger Syndrome (2001-2005)
podcast.body: Around 2001-2002, as The Vines gained traction in North America, Craig Nichols began exhibiting serious erratic behavior, including unusual habits like insisting on eating at McDonald's daily, and violent outbursts against journalists, audiences, and bandmates, which led to legal issues. He was officially diagnosed with Asperger's in 2005 and agreed to therapy. "We started hearing about some serious erratic behavior... In 2005, he was officially diagnosed in agreed to therapy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Asperger Syndrome Diagnosis and Assault Arrest
podcast.body: Craig Nicholls was properly diagnosed with Asperger Syndrome in 2005 and agreed to therapy, which initially showed success. However, in 2012, he was arrested for assaulting his parents, indicating ongoing challenges. "He was finally properly diagnosed in 2005 and agreed to therapy. That worked for a while, but then he was arrested for assaulting his parents in 2012."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bizarre Habits and Early Career Issues
podcast.body: When The Vines emerged in 2001, singer Craig Nicholls was noted for unusual behaviors, such as an insistence on eating at McDonald's at least once daily, a habit he maintains today, along with KFC. More significantly, he displayed severe temper issues directed at bandmates, journalists, photographers, fans, and strangers. "When the Vine's first appeared in 2001, we started hearing about Craig's bizarre habits, like insisting that he had to eat at McDonald's at least once a day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Coping Mechanisms
podcast.body: Currently, Craig Nichols manages his Asperger's by rarely going out, avoiding 21st-century technology, and dedicating as much time as possible to his music. "Now he does his best by rarely going out, staying away from any 21st century technology, spending as much time as he possibly can to his music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Current Hermetic Lifestyle
podcast.body: Presently, Craig Nicholls adheres to a strict lifestyle, avoiding wheat, abstaining from alcohol, and living largely in seclusion. He also minimizes his engagement with 21st-century technology. "Today, he stays away from wheat, doesn't drink, and lives rather hermetically while staying away from 21st century technology as much as he can."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Diagnosis Deterioration and Arrest
podcast.body: Despite initial therapy after his 2005 Asperger's diagnosis, Craig Nichols' condition deteriorated, leading to his arrest for assaulting his parents. "That worked for a while, but then he deteriorated again and was arrested for assaulting his parents."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tonight Show Incident and Legal Troubles
podcast.body: Craig Nicholls' temper led to the band being thrown off The Tonight Show after damaging J. Leno's set. These behavioral issues also resulted in legal problems and the sabotage of multiple tours for The Vines. "The band was even thrown off the tonight show for damaging part of J. Leno's set."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
